# xai and aiven: why every poll failed, and the fix (2026-11-09)

**Status: code fix written and gated (uncommitted, not deployed). Data repair SQL prepared, NOT run.**
This corrects the "identity drift" finding in `2026-11-09-disappearance-gap.md`. These two boards were never
refused by the liveness planner. **Their polls fail before liveness runs.** `company_watchlist.consecutive_failures`:
xai 45, aiven 20. `last_polled_at` moves on every failed attempt (`failureMark`, `_shared/ats/registry.ts:227`), and
`last_poll_job_count` keeps its old value (298 and 44). That made them look like "polled, 0 re-stamped".

## Cause

The probe replayed scout-ats's own read (`collectBoardPages` + `fetchBoard`, robots-gated; 5 GETs in total):

| Board | Live answer | Verdict from the repo's own code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| greenhouse `xai` | 200, 304 postings; every `company_name` = **"SpaceXSI"** | `evaluateBoardIdentity` → mismatch → `boardRefusal` = `identity_mismatch`; nothing persists |
| greenhouse `aiven36` | **404**; the plain token `aiven` is also 404 | an HttpError on every poll |

**It is still xAI's board:** 253 of the 291 stored Greenhouse job ids are live on it, and its links are
`job-boards.greenhouse.io/xai/jobs/...`. The provider renamed the company after the xAI/SpaceX merger. The identity
guard (the 2026-10-23 tcs→Thornbury control) did exactly its job: a renamed company is indistinguishable from a wrong
board until a person checks the ids.

**Duplicates so far: 0.** A refused poll persists nothing. The last inserts were xai 10-24 and aiven 10-27.

## Fix (code)

- `_shared/ats/identity.ts`: `BOARD_IDENTITY_ALIASES`, a closed list keyed by the BOARD (provider + token +
  watchlist name + the exact reported name). Its one row is `greenhouse / xai / xAI / SpaceXSI`.
  `evaluateBoardIdentity` takes the board token as an optional 4th argument. A caller that omits it gets no alias,
  which fails closed.
- `scout-ats/index.ts:427`: passes `board.board_token`.
- The watchlist name stays "xAI": the fingerprint is built from it (`registry.ts:245`), so renaming the row would
  re-key every posting.
- **Not covered:** `worker/src/cli/scout.ts:325` (peer 2's file) still calls without the token, so the worker
  keeps refusing xai. It is a one-line follow-up: pass `board.board_token`.

Tests (`identity.test.ts`, 4 new):
1. xai board + "SpaceXSI" → match.
2. Another token reporting "SpaceXSI" → mismatch.
3. The xai board reporting "Thornbury Community Services" → mismatch.
4. No token passed → mismatch.

Removing the alias row turns test 1 red; restored.

## What the first fixed poll would write (dry run with the scout's own `toJobInsert` + `firstPerFingerprint`)

304 live postings → 300 unique fingerprints:
- **116** match a stored fingerprint, so they are upserted onto the existing row;
- **184** are new inserts. **134 of them carry the same Greenhouse id as a stored row**: the posting was retitled
  ("Software Engineer - Evals" → "Software Engineer, Evals", some with "Sr." added), and the fingerprint is
  company + title + location, deliberately without the id. The other 50 are new postings.
- None of the 134 old rows has an application beyond `dropped_filter`. The one live xAI application (`0c9fdc58`,
  tailored) keeps its title, so it is upserted, not duplicated.

So without a repair the fix would create **134 duplicate rows by Greenhouse id**. They would be screened again,
though nothing could be applied to twice.

## Repair SQL (prepared, NOT run). Run it BEFORE deploying scout-ats

Re-key the 134 retitled rows onto the fingerprints the next poll will compute. Then those postings upsert onto
their existing rows (history and `first_seen_at` kept), and the first poll inserts only the 50 genuinely new ones.

Checked in the dry run:
- each Greenhouse id maps to exactly 1 stored row;
- no new fingerprint is already stored;
- no new fingerprint repeats.

The `old_fp` compare-and-set, plus the `not exists` check, make the statement a no-op for any row that changed or
would collide.

Expected effect: 134 rows updated. On the first poll the liveness overlap is (116 + 134) / 291 = 0.86, which passes
the drift guard. The 41 stored rows not on the board are 14% of it, below the 25% mass cap, so the planner marks
them gone.
